newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Thousands queue for new Hong Kong Chinese passport.
newsitem.headline: Thousands queue for new Hong Kong Chinese passport.

text.p: Thousands of prospective travellers formed long queues on Tuesday to apply for new Hong Kong passports to be issued as the British-ruled territory reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
China is allowing Hong Kong to issue its own passport because it will become a Special Administrative Region (SAR) with considerable autonomy.
Meanwhile many non-Chinese residents, mainly ethnic Indians and Pakistanis, will line up next week to apply for full British passports after a last-minute concession by London.
Queues built up by dawn outside Immigration headquarters in the bustling downtown Wanchai district for the travel documents to be issued after the historic handover of Hong Kong.
"We prepared 350,000 application forms for distribution today and tomorrow," a spokesman said. Some 40,000 had been distributed by late morning.
Three million of Hong Kong's 6.4 million population, 98 percent Chinese, are eligible to hold second-class British travel documents.
These are British National (Overseas) passports (BNO), which do not allow the holder to settle in Britain.
The BNO will remain valid beyond the handover, but many want to apply for the new passport as soon as possible.
The status of Hong Kong's non-Chinese residents remains unclear and it is not yet known if they are eligible for the Hong Kong passport, available to Chinese citizens of Hong Kong.
China considers all ethnic Chinese as citizens, irrespective of passport.

Minority residents include ethnic Indians and Pakistanis, whose families have lived in the British colony and thought of themselves as British for generations. They had feared being stateless after the handover and lobbied London for full passports with British residency rights.
Britain conceded their demands last February and says applications will be available from next Monday.
London envoy Francis Cornish told reporters the scheme aimed to answer the fears of an estimated 9,000 ethnic minorities who had no other nationality.

"This scheme is open to people who are British, solely British, and ordinarily resident in Hong Kong," he said. "Once you're registered, you will be eligible for a British citizen passport, the same passport that I've got."
